MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 15, 2019

  An adjourned meeting of the Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates
  was called to order at 6:00 p.m. at the George F Canyon Nature Center (Deck Area), 27305 Palos
  Verdes Drive East, Rolling Hills Estates, California by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI.

  2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Bain, Ciarolla, McCormick, Pope, Romanelli,
  Persichina

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  Retz

  STAFF PRESENT:  Andy Clark, Community Services Director
  Daniel A-Haja, Senior Recreation Leader
  Carol Corea, Administrative Assistant

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING DRAFT MINUTES OF
  MARCH 18, 2019

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK
  to:
  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF MARCH
  18, 2019.

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

  5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS NOT ON THE AGENDA

  None

  6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A.  STREET TREE REMOVAL APPLICATION – 50 RANCHVIEW ROAD (LIM)

  Community Services Director Clark stated that an application was submitted for the removal of
  two City street trees in front of property address 50 Ranchview Road. The trees have begun to lift
  the driveway.

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER BAIN, Community Services Director Clark stated
  that there is a setback from every curb, which varies street by street, that determines which trees
  are within the public right-of-way.

  Community Services Director stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities
  Commission approve the removal of two Shamel Ash street trees located at 50 Ranchview Road
  and the purchase of one 15-gallon California Pepper tree at the cost of the applicant.

  The Park and Activities Commission agreed to approve this request.

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  1
APRIL 15, 2019
   7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A.  REVISED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the park tours scheduled has been moved up by
  one month. However, if an item comes forward where it is not appropriate to hold the meeting at
  one of the parks, then the park tour will be postponed in order to hold the meeting in the Council
  Chamber.

  RECEIVED AND FILED

  B.  CONSIDERATION OF PROPOSED NAMES FOR “BUTCHER PARK”

  Community Services Director Clark stated that a few names were proposed by COMMISSION
  MCCORMICK and staff has proposed additional names as provided in the staff report. Due to a
  likely delay in the park development project, a decision on a prioritized list does not need to be
  determined at this meeting.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Park and Activities
  Commission consider and prioritize a list of appropriate names for the future park site currently
  known as “Butcher Park” for City Council’s consideration.

  In response to a question by COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN, Community Services Director Clark
  stated that Dan Butcher was the owner of the land.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER MCCORMICK inquired about community input on the name. Community
  Services Director Clark stated that this can still be explored.

  COMMITTEE MEMBER BAIN made a motion, seconded by COMMITTEE MEMBER CIAROLLA
  to,
  TABLE THIS ITEM TO DISCUSS AT A FUTURE PARK & ACTIVITIES COMMISSION
  MEETING.

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

  8.  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPERTREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD MEETING

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADVISORY BOARD
  MEETING

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

  A.  THE HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE START TIME

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI reported that the Race Subcommittee discussed changing the
  race time to 7:00 a.m., but there seemed to be no strong reason to change the race to an earlier
  time and changing the time would cause difficulty in securing volunteers. The Subcommittee also
  determined that there should be no change to the fee structure.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA further explained that the Subcommittee was not able to determine a
  feasible way to charge a family rate.

  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI added that there is $5 discount for purchasing tickets prior to the
  race. Community Services Director Clark also added that the combined cost of the race t-shirt
  and medal is approximately $9 per participant.

  A brief discussion ensued on fee options.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  2
APRIL 15, 2019
   COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER BAIN to,

  ESTABLISH A $100 FAMILY RATE.

  AYES:  BAIN, MCCORMICK
  NOES:  CIAROLLA, ROMANELLI, PERSICHINA
  ABSTAIN:  POPE
  ABSENT:  RETZ

  MOTION DENIED

  COMMISSIONER POPE made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA to,

  TO MAKE A RECOMMENDATION TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION TO
  ESTABLISH A FEE IF $10 FOR CHILDREN 10 AND UNDER FOR THE HILLS ARE
  ALIVE RACE.

  AYES:  BAIN, CIAROLLA, MCCORMICK, POPE, ROMANELLI, PERSICHINA
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:  RETZ

  MOTION CARRIES

  B.  NATURE CENTER DECK AWNINGS REPLACEMENT

  Community Service Director Clark provided a summary of the staff report for this item.

  Community Services Director Clark stated that staff recommends that the Pepper Tree
  Foundation Advisory Board make a recommendation to the Pepper Tree Foundation Board of
  Director’s to approve the replacement of the George F Canyon Nature Center’s back deck
  awnings at a cost not exceed $6,028.00.

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  APPROVE STAFF’S RECOMMENDATION.

  AYES:  BAIN, CIAROLLA, MCCORMICK, POPE, ROMANELLI, PERSICHINA
  NOES:
  ABSTAIN:
  ABSENT:  RETZ

  MOTION CARRIES

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER BAIN, Community Services Director Clark stated
  that the awning will be dark green.

  9.  RECONVENE TO PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING

  VICE CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to,

  RECONVENE TO THE PARK AND ACITIVITIES COMMITTEE MEETING

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

  10.  COMMISSION ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS

  COMMISSIONER POPE inquired about the tree that was removed near the plaque at Silver Spur
  Park. Community Services Director Clark stated that he will follow-up on this.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  3
APRIL 15, 2019
   11.  DIRECTOR’S ITEMS (Verbal Reports)

  A.  EARTH DAY CELEBRATION – APRIL 17, 2019

  B.  MAYOR’S BREAKFAST RIDE – MAY 4, 2019

  Community Services Director reminded anyone who would needs to rent a horse to please let
  him know and also encouraged the commission to purchase breakfast ride tickets (available now
  at City Hall).

  C.  BEER AND WINE FESTIVAL – MAY 19, 2019

  Community Services Director Clark stated that the event fee will not go into effect until July and
  the organizers have made aware that there will be a $1 per participant fee next year.

  D.  PALOS VERDES PENINSULA STREET FAIR AND MUSIC FESTIVAL – JUNE 8-9, 2019

  Community services Director Clark stated that at the next meeting, Daniel A-Haja will have a
  volunteer sign-up sheet.

  12.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A.  PLANNING COMMISSION DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 4, 2019

  B.  EQUESTRIAN COMMITTEE DRAFT MINUTES OF MARCH 25, 2019

  RECEIVED AND FILED

  13.  FUTURE AGENDA ITEMS

  A.  PARK USE REGULATION REVISIONS

  B.  PALOS VERDES NORTH MEDIANS LANDSCAPING PROJECT

  In response to a question by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI, Community Services Director Clark
  stated that at the Policy Development meeting, it was discussed that they would like to replicate
  the look of the median from west of city hall to the west side of the city and consider the same in
  front of City Hall to Rolling Hills Road. This will be discussed further at a future meeting.

  14.  PARK TOURS

  The Park and Activities Commissioners toured the George F Canyon Nature Center.

  No comments were made.

  The Park and Activities Commissioners toured the future site of Taber Grove. They determined
  the portion of land where the park will end on the west end and will have the Maintenance
  Supervisor delineate the agreed upon area.

  The Park and Activities Commissioners toured Dapplegray Park.

  No comments were made.

  There was no tour of “Butcher Park” due to it being used as a staging area for the CalWater
  project.

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  4
APRIL 15, 2019
   15.  ADJOURNMENT

  COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER PERSICHINA
  to,

  ADJOURN THE MEETING TO THE NEXT ADJOURNED PARK AND ACTIVITIES
  MEETING ON MAY 20, 2019 AT 6:00 P.M., WHICH WILL MEET AT CITY HALL
  FOLLOWED BY PARK TOURS OF PEPPERWOOD, CHANDLER, ROCKBLUFF, AND
  SILVER SPUR PARKS.

  There being no objection, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI so ordered.

  Respectfully submitted,  Approved,

  __________________________  _____________________________
  Carol Corea  Heidi Luce
  Administrative Assistant  City Clerk

PARK AND ACTIVITIES MEETING MINUTES,  5
APRIL 15, 2019
